episode.question: I changed one number in a registered document. Could HPS detect it?
episode.experiment: Change the Amount paid field from $74.34 to $70.00 and verify only the candidate document.

scenes.headline: I changed one number in a registered document. Could HPS detect it?
scenes.body: The candidate was classified as RELATED / MODIFIED.
scenes.narration: Here is the question: I changed one number in a registered document. Could HPS detect it? The candidate was classified as RELATED / MODIFIED. I wanted to see what would happen when the file was actually tested.

scenes.headline: Change one thing. Keep everything else stable.
scenes.body: Change the Amount paid field from $74.34 to $70.00.
scenes.narration: The setup is simple. Start with the registered object, change one controlled field, and keep everything else as close as possible.

scenes.headline: One small edit can carry a large meaning.
scenes.narration: Now for the change. The Amount paid field moved from $74.34 to $70.00. Visually small. Semantically important.

scenes.headline: Identity first. Relationship second.
scenes.body: Exact SHA-256 answers whether the bytes are identical. Resilient fingerprints help determine whether a changed file is still related.
scenes.narration: HPS separates exact identity from resilient relationship evidence.

scenes.headline: Relationship confidence was 79%.
scenes.narration: The candidate stayed strongly related, but the strict canonical text did not match.

scenes.headline: Related does not mean identical.
scenes.body: A high relationship score should not be interpreted as proof that the candidate content is unchanged.
scenes.narration: A strong relationship can coexist with a meaningful edit.

scenes.headline: Provenance is not the same thing as truth.
scenes.body: HPS establishes provenance and integrity evidence; it does not prove that every factual statement inside a document is true.
scenes.narration: This is a hard boundary in the claim.

scenes.headline: Digital files move through messy real-world workflows.
scenes.body: Sharing, conversion, OCR, screenshots and editing all leave different traces.
scenes.narration: Real documents do not remain pristine.

scenes.headline: Stop asking: Does this look official?
scenes.body: Start asking: Can the claimed source prove it issued this exact or related object?
scenes.narration: The larger shift is from appearance to evidence.

scenes.headline: What should we try to break next?
scenes.body: Documents. Images. Screenshots. AI-generated content. Research outputs.
scenes.narration: Subscribe and tell me what digital object I should stress-test next.

shorts.title: Related does not mean identical
shorts.hook: A high similarity score can still hide an important edit.
shorts.script: A file can remain strongly related to the original while a material value changes.

shorts.title: Stop trusting letterheads
shorts.hook: A logo can look official and still tell you nothing about origin.
shorts.script: The better question is whether the claimed issuer can prove its relationship to the digital object.
